comparator.name: Bachelor Brain Science
comparator.academicYear: 2025-2026 official Education and Examination Regulations (the current formally adopted regulation governing the programme's module and credit structure; checked 2026-09-28), independently corroborated by the current official 2025-2026 course catalogue for individual course content, prerequisites and teaching periods and by current official overview, courses-and-curriculum, minors, why-this-programme and your-future page content for the Fall-2026 entrant cohort (checked 2026-09-28); the interactive curriculum.maastrichtuniversity.nl portal and its linked Mendix course-repository application that would normally host a browsable current-year curriculum view could not be parsed by available tools, so the static official EER and course-catalogue PDFs were used instead
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed primarily from the official Education and Examination Regulations Bachelor Brain Science 2025-2026 (s3: maastrichtuniversity.nl/file/finaleerbachelorbrsc2025-2026pdf), the single formally adopted document that lays out the complete year-1-to-year-3 module and credit structure for the current cohort. Its Article 3.6 'Composition' overview tables give the exact module names, ECTS credits and period placement for years 1 and 2, and its year-3 overview table establishes that year 3 consists of a 30-EC elective/minor package in periods 1-3, two period-4 compulsory courses (A Transdisciplinary View on Computational Modelling, 4 EC, and Current Trends and Critical Reading in Brain Science, 4 EC), a year-long 1-EC Mentor-guided Portfolio Building component, and a period-6 21-EC Bachelor's Thesis Project; these year-3 figures (30+4+4+1+21=60 EC) are independently corroborated by Article 3.7's Minor rule that 'the minor has a study load of at least 30 credits' and by Article 3.8/5.9's confirmation that the programme's third year proceeds to the bachelor's thesis. Individual year-1 and year-2 course names, OSIRIS codes, exact ECTS credits, periods and content are corroborated by the official 2025-2026 course catalogue (s2: maastrichtuniversity.nl/file/fpn-course-catalog-2025-20264502babrainsciencepdf), which lists every BRAIN1xxx/BRAIN2xxx course with its own credit and period fields; the two sources' year-1 and year-2 figures agree exactly (60 EC in each year). The curriculum.maastrichtuniversity.nl portal that would normally host an interactive current-year 'Courses & curriculum' overview and its linked courserepository.maastrichtuniversity.nl application are both dynamic, JavaScript-rendered tools that available tools could not extract structured data from; the two official PDFs above were used instead as they are static, complete and current. No formally named route, track or specialization exists within the Bachelor Brain Science itself: the programme is a single unified curriculum in years 1 and 2, and its only genuine internal choice point is the year-3 elective/minor package, which Article 3.7 confirms is drawn from an entirely different UM faculty or Dutch university (not a Brain-Science-internal specialization), from a fixed menu of ten named minors published on the official minors page (s6: maastrichtuniversity.nl/brain-science): Arts and Heritage, European Studies and Gender and Diversity Studies (FASoS), Globalisation and Development and Great Thinkers: Leading Paradigms of Western Culture (FASoS), Sustainable Healthcare (FHML), European Public Health (FHML), Health Sciences (FHML), Sustainability (SBE), and Art, Law and Policy Making (FoL/FASoS/FSE); s6 confirms that 'Students of the programme Brain Science may only follow 30 ECTS minors', i.e. must complete the full 30-EC version of whichever minor they choose. Because this is genuine external, student-selectable open space rather than an internal Brain Science route or a fixed set of named content, Section 2.1's route-selection hierarchy does not apply and no route is recorded; the 30 EC are instead preserved explicitly as their own comparator component (y3-01) rather than arbitrarily instantiating one of the ten minors as though it were the whole target. Programme orientation, disciplinary framing ('combining knowledge of Psychology, Biology and Computational Science'), and graduate-outcome context are corroborated by the current official overview, why-this-programme and your-future pages (s0, s4, s5) and the courses-and-curriculum landing page (s1), checked 2026-09-28. Voltijd delivery starting once yearly in September (s0) matches the fixed Fall-2026 UCR cohort. Every component's exact EC weight is taken directly from the EER's and catalogue's own per-module ECTS fields; the year-1, year-2 and year-3 subtotals each sum to exactly 60 EC, for a complete 180-EC reconstruction.

alternatives.label: Brain Science: Integrating Psychology, Biology and Computational Modelling of the Brain
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is evenly distributed across UCR's own psychology/cognitive-neuroscience cluster (8 of 24: Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Neurobiology, Perception & Action, Higher Order Functions, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Abnormal Psychology, Advanced Research Seminar, Lifespan Developmental Psychology), biological/life-science cluster (7 of 24: Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Molecular Cell Biology, Biochemistry, Life Science Laboratory, Functional Anatomy, Epidemiology & Public Health, Molecular Pathology & Genetics), and mathematics/computational cluster (7 of 24: Introduction to Programming, Mathematical Methods, Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Machine Learning, Advanced Calculus), plus Ethics and PPD. This near-even three-way split directly mirrors the target's own repeated self-description as combining Psychology, Biology and Computational Science, so the label names all three disciplines rather than letting one strand dominate.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to the Bachelor Brain Science: a transdisciplinary programme built from UCR's own psychology/cognitive-neuroscience cluster (brain-and-behaviour gateway, cellular neurobiology, perception, higher cognitive functions), biological/life-science cluster (molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, laboratory technique, functional anatomy, epidemiology, molecular genetics), and mathematics/computational cluster (programming, linear algebra, calculus, probability and statistics, machine learning and deep learning), reinforced by ethics and PPD -- reproducing the target's own combination of psychological, biological and computational perspectives on the brain and its own quantitative/experimental research-methods training, while leaving the target's own specialist neuroimaging-methods, biophysical-modelling, motor-system and cellular/systems-memory depth, and its supervised project placements and thesis, genuinely unmatched, since UCR offers no equivalent placement-based research training or that level of specialist computational-neuroscience depth.
progression: HCBGATE101 and HCBGATE102 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precede every course in semesters 2-6 that formally requires them: HCBLIFE211 and HCBBIOM211 (semester 2, require HCBGATE101), HCBLIFE213 (semester 3, requires HCBGATE101), HCBCOGN311 (semester 3, requires HCBGATE102), HCBCOGN212 and HCBPSYC212 and HCBPSYC313 (semester 4, require HCBGATE102), HCBLIFE311 (semester 5, requires HCBGATE101), and HCBLIFE214 and HCBPSYC314 (semester 6, require HCBGATE102). DISGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes every course that formally requires it: DISMATH211 (semester 3), DISDATA311 (semester 4), and DISMATH314 (semester 5). Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Gateway and level-1/level-2 foundational courses (Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Introduction to Programming, Mathematical Methods, Neurobiology, Molecular Cell Biology, Functional Anatomy, Biochemistry, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Linear Algebra, Perception & Action, Abnormal Psychology, Epidemiology & Public Health, Machine Learning) are concentrated in semesters 1-4, and level-3 advanced work (Higher Order Functions, Advanced Research Seminar, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Probability & Statistics, Lifespan Developmental Psychology) is concentrated in semesters 3-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternatives.label: Population and Public Health: From Brain and Behavioural Health to Health Systems and Policy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's social-science, policy and economics cluster (8 of 24: Introduction to Sociology, Qualitative Research Methodology, Modern Sociology, Theory of International Relations, Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Economics, Public Economics, Sustainability Essentials I), grounded in a substantial biomedical-disease foundation (6 of 24: Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Epidemiology & Public Health, Pharmacology, Infection & Immunity, Mechanisms of Disease, Human Physiology) and a health-psychology cluster (7 of 24: Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Abnormal Psychology, Medical & Health Psychology, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology), plus Ethics, Communication and PPD. The label names population and public health first for the dominant social/policy/economics cluster's applied focus, and health systems and policy second because the retained biomedical and psychological grounding exists specifically to ground that population-health perspective in real disease and behavioural-health content.
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second UCR route evidenced by the target's own formal Sustainable Healthcare, European Public Health, Health Sciences and Sustainability minor options (all offered to Brain Science students at other UM faculties): a programme that studies disease mechanisms, pharmacology and health psychology only far enough to ground them, then applies UCR's full available sociology, international-relations, economics and sustainability curriculum to population-level and public-health perspectives on preventing disease and organising health systems -- studying how individual brain and bodily health connects to population health, social context and health-systems policy, rather than studying the brain's own molecular, computational and cognitive-neuroscience mechanisms for their own sake as in the closest match.
progression: HCBGATE101 and HCBGATE102 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precede every course in later semesters that formally requires them: HCBBIOM312 (semester 2, requires HCBGATE101), HCBBIOM311, HCBLIFE212 and HCBPSYC311 (semester 3, require HCBGATE101/HCBGATE102 respectively), HCBBIOM313 and HCBPSYC212 and HCBPSYC312 (semester 4, require HCBGATE101/HCBGATE102), and HCBPSYC314 (semester 6, requires HCBGATE102). BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENECON311 (semester 4), which formally requires it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Gateway and level-1/level-2 foundational courses (Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Introduction to Sociology, Research Methods & Statistics, Infection & Immunity, Qualitative Research Methodology, Pharmacology, Human Physiology, Medical & Health Psychology, Modern Sociology) are concentrated in semesters 1-3, and level-3 advanced work (Public Economics, Mechanisms of Disease, Abnormal Psychology, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies, Lifespan Developmental Psychology) is concentrated in semesters 4-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: The closest match retains a comprehensive 8-course psychology/cognitive-neuroscience cluster and a 7-course mathematics/computational cluster addressing the brain's own molecular and computational mechanisms. This alternative goes materially further: it shares only 8 of 24 courses with the closest match (Personal & Professional Development, Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Epidemiology & Public Health, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Abnormal Psychology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Ethics -- a deliberately retained grounding, since a defensible population-health concept must still be built on real biomedical and behavioural-health content) and replaces the remaining 16 of the closest match's courses (Introduction to Programming, Mathematical Methods, Neurobiology, Molecular Cell Biology, Higher Order Functions, Biochemistry, Linear Algebra, Perception & Action, Advanced Research Seminar, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Probability & Statistics, Machine Learning, Life Science Laboratory, Advanced Calculus, Functional Anatomy) with 16 UCR sociology, international-relations, economics, sustainability, communication and clinical-health-psychology courses entirely absent from the closest match. This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from studying the brain's own molecular, computational and cognitive mechanisms directly to studying how disease, treatment and behavioural health connect to population health, social context and health-systems policy, and the two alternatives differ in 16 of 24 courses each way (120 EC each way), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum.
traceOverrides: trains foundational statistical and experimental methods, directly implementing the population-health direction's own research-methods and data-analysis requirement (in this alternative complementing, rather than contributing to, computational modelling, which this alternative's evidence map does not draw on)

candidates.label: Great Thinkers: Leading Paradigms of Western Culture

selection.assessment: The closest match directly owns sixteen generator-eligible rows describing the programme's own transdisciplinary psychological, biological and computational identity, its research-methods training, its ethics content and its culminating independent research (5593, 5594, 5595, 5596, 5597, 5598, 5599, 5600, 5601, 5609, 5610, 5611, 5612, 5613, 5614, 5615). These describe the programme's own general brain-science identity rather than an independent substantive direction, and are therefore substantively covered by the closest match's own core concept rather than forced into a residual candidate. The nine remaining generator-eligible rows are all Stable study direction rows naming the ten formal minors available to Brain Science students at other faculties. Four of them cluster around a genuinely coherent, evidence-backed population/public-health direction -- Sustainable Healthcare (5620), European Public Health (5621), Health Sciences (5622) and Sustainability (5623) -- reinforced by the curricular-topic rows on Parkinson's/Alzheimer's disease and CNS injury and recovery (5607, 5608) and by the outcome row on brain science in healthcare (5626). This candidate passes all four gates: it is evidence-backed by four target-specific Stable study direction rows; it has a clear organising logic (population-level and public-health approaches to disease prevention and health systems rather than studying the brain's own mechanisms for their own sake); it is substantively distinct, replacing 16 of the closest match's 24 courses (120 EC) with UCR's full available sociology, international-relations, economics and sustainability curriculum while retaining only the biomedical and behavioural-health grounding the concept itself requires; and it is mechanically feasible against the enriched course database, with six distinct level-300 courses and a pairwise difference of 16 courses (120 EC) against the closest match. Production therefore includes it as the second alternative. The remaining five Stable study direction rows were each independently assessed and rejected as insufficient-evidence: Great Thinkers: Leading Paradigms of Western Culture (5619) names only a broad intellectual-history minor with no specific connection to the brain, mind or any evidenced Brain Science topic, so a full 24-course programme built around it would require importing untethered humanities content rather than extending the target's own evidenced field; Arts and Heritage (5616) similarly names only a visual/material-culture and archaeology minor with no evidenced connection to the target's own content; Gender and Diversity Studies (5617) names only a gender-studies minor with no evidenced connection to the target's own content; Globalisation and Development (5618) names only an international-development-studies minor with no evidenced connection to the target's own content; and Art, Law and Policy Making (5624) names only an interdisciplinary arts/law/policy minor with no evidenced connection to the target's own content. Each of these five rows establishes only that the named minor is formally available to Brain Science students, not that it represents a defensible academic extension of the programme's own evidenced field, interests, questions or applications; treating any of them as generative would require substituting most non-PPD courses with content unconnected to the evidenced core field, which Section 2.2 forbids. No further generator-eligible evidence remains: every generator-eligible row is now owned by either the closest match or the second alternative, and no unclustered generator-eligible row or coherent combination of curricular-topic support-only rows remains available to organise an independent third concept without duplicating one of the two included directions or relying on an omnibus residual bucket. Production therefore stops at two alternatives and records insufficient-evidence as the stopping reason for a third.

notes.text: Both UCR alternatives include substantial study of brain disorders and disease mechanisms. The Bachelor Brain Science programme additionally includes specialist Measuring and Manipulating Brain Activity training (EEG, MEG, fMRI, TMS, tDCS/tACS), Biophysical Modelling of ion channels and neural populations, and a supervised third-year Bachelor's Thesis Project. UCR students can instead combine Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Advanced Calculus and (in the second alternative) UCR's standardised Optional independent research opportunity, but UCR offers no dedicated neuroimaging-methods laboratory training, ion-channel-level biophysical modelling, or supervised thesis placement of that kind.

The Bachelor Brain Science programme organises its third year primarily around a freely chosen 30-EC minor at another faculty or university, two compulsory computational/critical-reading courses, and a supervised thesis. The second UCR alternative instead organises the equivalent profiling space around population and public health, drawing on UCR's own sociology, international-relations, economics and sustainability curriculum. The two programmes therefore cover related health-related ground through substantially different curricular structures in their profiling space rather than one reproducing the other course by course.

The Bachelor Brain Science programme's third-year elective/minor package is genuine open space that a student fills with one of ten unrelated minors (from Arts and Heritage to Health Sciences). No single UCR course or course combination can defensibly represent this space, since its actual content depends entirely on the individual student's choice; the comparison therefore preserves it explicitly as open elective space rather than inventing or arbitrarily selecting content for it.
